objective: Run the model-form matrix on the ERCOFTAC periodic hills, the standing batch's four closure families on the medium rung of our own verified mesh, to learn whether any closure enters the literature reattachment band and whether the inter-model band contains it
rationale: The hills closed with a physics FAIL, reattachment 72 percent long against the literature band, and the failure was verified onto the model rather than onto us: our own mesh agrees with the shipped grid to 0.043 percent with 0.097 percent grid sensitivity. What the verdict taught is that SST overpredicts separated-region length on the hills the same way it does on the hump, a two-leg pattern. The standing model-form batch already runs four closure families on other cases; extending its family set to the hills asks the two questions the verdict left open, whether any closure enters the band and whether the inter-model band contains the reference, and feeds the epistemic-uncertainty showcase directly.
gate: Four solves, one per closure family, on the medium rung of the verified in-house hills mesh, each read against the published reattachment band under outcomes declared before launch. Outcome one: at least one closure lands inside the literature band, which locates the failure in closure choice rather than in the class. Outcome two: none does but the inter-model band contains the reference, which is the epistemic-uncertainty result. Outcome three: even the inter-model band excludes the reference, which is a class-level finding. No scoring call is made; the matrix reports whichever outcome the runs deliver
cost_basis: estimate, the review's own figure: four closures at the medium rung of a ladder whose rungs this campaign has already run and logged, so the per-solve price is anchored to the family's recorded spend rather than to a guess
expected_knowledge_gain: Either a closure that works on the hills, which redirects the two-leg separated-flow finding from the class to the closure, or a measured inter-model band whose relation to the reference is exactly what the epistemic-uncertainty showcase needs from its training-class flow

decision_note: Approved by the chief 223c3b84 (negative-verdict review entry 1); executed by the Cases family supervisor as standing model-form family H, pre-registered 28e14422 before launch.
outcome: Executed 2026-08-08 at 29.18 of 35 core-min on the verified F6b medium mesh -- COMPLIANT (non-ortho 39.66 vs 70), R12 not needed and not invoked. Per-member under the pre-registered uniform gate: kOmegaSST ADMITTED (x_R 7.647235, the archived 7.6472 reproduced to 0.0005 percent); SpalartAllmaras EXCLUDED (12000-cap without residualControl, 0 crossings, residuals still descending -- slow, not plateaued); kEpsilon EXCLUDED (S1 FPE at iteration 13, the family-B high-Re k-family crash class now on the hills); realizableKE EXCLUDED (cap, 0 crossings, still descending). Entry-1 answers: no closure is measured inside the Rapp/Breuer/Froehlich band [4.21, 4.70] -- the only measured closure sits at +72 percent -- and the band-containment question is REFUSED at n=1 (no band exists; first live application of the filed no-containment-verdict-below-n3 rule, applied by pre-registration). The measured finding: the inter-model band methodology hits a family-convergence wall on the hills, the bump's family-B pattern on a second separated case. Successors recommended, not run: an extension arm for the two still-descending members (30000 cap, own pre-registration -- an adjusted criterion is NOT the right rescue, the targets look reachable), and a family-B-style FPE diagnosis arm for kEpsilon. Full record: campaign/MODEL_FORM_H_HILLS_PREREGISTRATION.md outcome section; band artifact group H_re10595.
